reviews.text: They have a cute Samoyed named Momon-chan. The staff are also very friendly.
It's so relaxing to see a large dog wandering around the store, and the staff are so kind!

The monkey and adult cat are sitting in tiny cages. The cat was crying the entire rime we were in the store. An adult cat should not be kept in a small wire cage with no place to hide. Do not support this place.

I am a foreigner who doesn't know Japanese. Despite the language barrier, the staff tried to communicate with me through Google translate. The experience was great and I got what I was looking for. The staff was quite sincere and helpful.

A shop with inadequate crisis management.
There was a large, unleashed dog in the treatment room (a closed room) where they trim the bird's nails, as mentioned in other reviews. The staff didn't notice and took the bird out of its cage. I was extremely worried when I realized the dog was there during the treatment.
There were two staff members, but neither noticed. They apologized when I told them on my way out, but...it was terrifying. The older man who seemed to be the manager was acting ineffectively, so that might have been part of the problem.

Nine years ago, I welcomed a cinnamon finch chick into my home at this store. He's exactly nine years old now, but he's still going strong. He even used the alarm sound from my cell phone as a phrase in a song he wrote himself. He's so cute.
The store was quite small, but the finch chick became very attached to the staff.
The parakeet chicks were aggressive to a level I've never seen before. The access was poor and it was a waste of time. The telephone service was also terrible.
The explanation given by the store clerk was very clear and easy to understand.

I happened to stop by. The extremely poor condition of the store was shocking.
Thinking about the animals I saw there makes me very sad.
The conditions were so bad that I'm seriously considering reporting it to the authorities.

▼Condition on the 1st Floor
- The store faces a bus stop, and many tourists come and go throughout the day, some on video calls and others drinking alcohol.
- Immediately upon entering the store, there was a cat in a small, unclean cage.
- The store's air conditioning was not properly controlled that day.
- The merchandise was covered in dust.
- A large dog was placed in the cash register area, but it was left unattended without being secured by a leash or anything. (Apparently, it was the store's mascot dog.)
- Dogs and cats were haphazardly housed in cages.
- The entire store lacked cleanliness and smelled terrible.

▼Condition on the 2nd Floor
- Meerkats were displayed haphazardly immediately upon climbing the stairs.

- The stench was terrible even before reaching the top of the stairs; it was unbearable even for humans, so it must have been extremely bad for the animals.

- A continuous "woof" sound was heard coming from the back room. It didn't sound like a dog.

- A Shiba Inu was not kept in a cage but was tied up in the room.

- There was no water dispenser or toilet facilities, and it was wearing a diaper.

- It was so listless and lethargic that I didn't notice it until I got close.

- The leash was very short, and it was in an environment where it couldn't move around properly.

- To reiterate, the birds, meerkats, and fish were all kept in dirty cages or tanks.

- A strong stench permeated the first floor and above, making the sanitary environment extremely unsuitable.

This is not a matter of customer service, but clearly requires a review of the store's operations and management.

The animals are not in a condition to be sold, and the living conditions are extremely poor.
I am grateful that the staff have always been so supportive and helpful.
Small exotic animals are kept in the cage upstairs. It’s terrible and this place should be shut down.

On January 4, 2016,

Reiko Sasa took me to this store.

It was so much fun! They have all kinds of rare animals and lizards, even though they're rare in Japan!!! The prices are in line with their rarity. ☆◇

I don't speak English, but if I ask the staff in Japanese, I might be able to see some babies.
